text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing an uptick in gRPC stream resets for long-lived inference sessions from hosted-edge through the egress proxy in us-west-2. ~9% of sessions hit RST/STREAM within 30-90s :eyes:
aj: timeline? any deploys or infra changes?
maria: started ~07:26 UTC, coincides with a small autoscale event on dedicated pools but not sure that's causal. No prod deploys.
kevin: I see similar on dashboards — connection churn goes up and average active streams per worker drops. Traces point at edge-proxy (envoy) between ALB and our frontend.
lina: can you paste a sample spike log?
maria: snippet from proxy logs (envoy) — lots of: 
```
[2025-11-02T07:27:14Z] info stream_id=34567 stream_reset: code=STREAM_CONNECTION_ERROR details="stream aborted by remote" upstream:10.1.5.23:443
```
aj: interesting. upstream kept-alive looks fine? netstat on frontend shows many connections in CLOSE_WAIT/TIME_WAIT from egress IP pool. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion + connection ownership flip.
kevin: ran tcpdump on client side during a repro: lots of FIN then new SYNs to same ephemeral ports -> some connection reuse/translation weirdness at NAT.
lina: NAT table size on the egress gateway at the time?
maria: opsbot reports conntrack at 99% at 07:25-07:30.
opsbot: conntrack_count=999812 max=1000000 threshold=0.9998 (host: egress-gw-3)
aj: that matches. When conntrack saturates, kernel starts dropping state and we see mid-stream resets when NAT mapping disappears. But why only for long streams?
kevin: because long streams keep state longer; also HTTP/2 multiplexing means single TCP connection carries many streams — if the NAT mapping for that 5-tuple is evicted weird things occur when packets arrive later.
lina: check keepalive settings between clients and edge-proxy. If idle timeouts shorter than conntrack, socket state could be dropped from kernel while app thinks it exists.
maria: our envoy config uses http2 settings: keepalive_idle: 60s, http2_max_concurrent_streams: 100. Kernel conntrack default timeout for ESTABLISHED maybe 432000s, but UDP/tcp mappings varied due to port reuse script and iptables SNAT.
aj: also saw evidence of connection 'ownership' flipping in NAT logs — SNAT hash is reassigning ephemeral ports to new upstreams while old streams still active, causing packets to appear from different internal hosts.
kevin: repro path: start 1 long stream, then flood many short streams to force ephemeral reuse + conntrack churn => long stream gets RESET.
lina: mitigation options: increase conntrack table, tune nf_conntrack hashsize, add persistent mapping for edge-proxy IPs, or move to per-worker egress IP (avoid SNAT collisions). Which is least intrusive?
maria: ops suggests increment conntrack and roll egress-gw update with larger table and sysctl: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000 temporarily.
aj: we also should add socket keepalive lower on long-lived worker-client side (30s) so NAT sees activity. But careful: extra keepalives increase load.
kevin: another quick fix: make ALB use TCP proxy protocol to preserve connection origin and reduce SNAT churn? that needs infra change.
lina: rolling conntrack bump now on egress-gw-3,4,5. ops: please monitor ephemeral port usage and stream reset rate.
opsbot: started conntrack bump job at 07:45 UTC. changeset id: egress-20251107-ctbump
maria: also adding a short diagnostic: script that hits long stream every 20s to keep NAT mapping alive for repro and to validate mitigation.
aj: let's hold on more invasive LB changes until we see if conntrack bump + keepalive tweaks reduce resets. If not, follow-up: per-node egress IPs.
kevin: noted. Will create a runbook with reproduction steps, metrics to watch (conntrack_count, stream_reset_rate, TIME_WAIT), and roll-back plan. Assigning to eng-platform oncall to track during office hours. :memo:
maria: thanks team — will update thread if resets drop after bump. :thumbsup:
